name: vm-list
description: List the running Snow emulators that have MCP on: name, PID, folder, workspace.

name: vm-wait
description: Wait until a Snow emulator is running (up) or has ended (gone).

name: vm-info
description: Describe the machine: model, run state, speed, RAM, screen size, mouse mode, floppy drives, SCSI targets (disks, CD-ROMs, Ethernet and its link). Use it first.

name: vm-power
description: pause or resume the CPU, reset the machine, or quit Snow (quit first writes the disks back, like the Quit command).

name: vm-speed
description: Set the emulation speed. accurate: real hardware speed. dynamic: real speed while sound plays, else as fast as possible. uncapped: as fast as possible, no sound (good for installs). video: 60 frames a second, no sound. fastforward: up to 'factor' times real speed.

factor.description: For fastforward: the most times real speed (default: 4)

name: screenshot
description: A PNG of the emulated screen. Coordinates in all tools are screen pixels, origin top-left.

scale.description: Zoom factor, e.g. 2 for small text (default: 1)

pointer.description: Mark where the tools last put the mouse pointer with a red cross

name: wait-screen
description: Wait until the screen changes, settles, or both, instead of sleeping. Changes of fewer than min-pixels pixels (a blinking text cursor) do not count. One call can wait up to 25 minutes.

stable-ms.description: How long the screen must stay the same (default: 1000)

timeout-ms.description: Give up after this long (default: 30000, at most 1500000)

region.description: Watch only this part of the screen

ignore.description: Parts of the screen to leave out, such as a clock

min-pixels.description: A change must touch more pixels than this (default: 32)

screenshot.description: Add a screenshot when done (default: true)

name: key
description: Press keys. Each entry is a key or a combination: 'return', 'cmd+o', 'cmd+shift+3', 'option+e', 'tab', 'esc', 'left', 'f1', 'kp5', 'a', '?'. Names: cmd, shift, option, control, capslock, return, enter (keypad), tab, space, delete (backspace), forwarddelete, escape, left, right, up, down, help, home, end, pageup, pagedown, power, f1-f15, clear, kp0-kp9, kp. kp* kp+ kp- kp/ kp=. The Mac's Command key is cmd.

keys.description: A key or combination, or a list of them pressed one after another

hold-ms.description: How long to hold each combination (default: 60)

name: type-text
description: Type text on the US keyboard layout. \n types Return, \t Tab. Characters that are not on the US layout are refused before anything is typed.

name: mouse-move
description: Move the mouse pointer to a screen pixel. Needs the Absolute mouse mode (Snow's default) and a booted Mac OS.

name: mouse-click
description: Click (or double-click) the mouse button at a screen pixel. Without x and y it clicks where the pointer is.

hold-ms.description: How long the button stays down (default: 100)

name: mouse-drag
description: Press the button at one pixel, move to another in steps, and let go. Also for pull-down menus: drag from the menu title to the item.

hold-ms.description: Wait this long with the button down at the start, e.g. for a menu to open (default: 150)

name: mouse-button
description: Press or release the mouse button, optionally after moving to a pixel. For drags the other tools don't cover.

name: media
description: Change media. insert-floppy (path, drive, write-protect), eject-floppy (drive), attach-disk (id, path: a hard disk image), attach-cdrom (id, path optional), load-cdrom (id, path), attach-ethernet (id), ethernet-link (id, link: down, nat or nat-https), detach (id). Paths are on the host; relative ones start in Snow's working folder.

name: clipboard-read
description: The text on the Mac's clipboard (the scrap). Copy something in the guest first (cmd+c); a good way to read text without reading pixels.

name: serial-write
description: Send bytes to a serial port, as if they came over the cable. Port a is the modem port, b the printer port. Has no effect while a serial bridge uses the port.

name: serial-read
description: What the Mac sent on a serial port since the last serial-read or serial-expect (or, with all, everything kept).

name: serial-expect
description: Wait until the Mac sends some text on a serial port.

name: steps
description: Run several tool calls in one: [{"tool": "mouse-click", "args": {...}}, ...]. Stops at the first call that fails or at a wait that is not met. Only the last screenshot is returned.

name: debug-registers
description: The 68k registers and the code at the PC.

name: debug-run
description: Let the CPU run until a breakpoint (or the until address) is hit, then show the registers. Pause it with vm-power pause.

until.description: Stop at this address (a breakpoint only for this run)

name: debug-step
description: Run single instructions while the CPU is stopped: into, over (a subroutine or trap) or out (to the caller).

name: debug-break
description: Breakpoints: add or remove one at an address or on an A-line trap (by name like _Open or SCSIDispatch, or opcode A000), list, or clear all. When one is hit the CPU stops; debug-registers shows where.

name: debug-traps
description: Record the Mac OS system traps (A-line calls) the guest makes: start, do the thing, read (the last count, optionally only lines that contain filter), stop.

filter.description: Only lines that contain this, e.g. Open or SCSI

name: memory-read
description: Hex dump of guest memory (?? for bytes that can't be read).

view.description: Default: virtual (as the CPU's data reads see it)

name: memory-write
description: Write bytes to guest memory.

name: disassemble
description: Disassemble 68k code, with Mac OS trap names.
